A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEEK watermarking research. All 30 pages of v1 and 37 pages of v2, including figures, equations, appendices A–I and v2's added checklist, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original watermark detection, scrubbing and spoofing experiments, text-quality measurements, and appendix evaluations across models, decoding strategies and copy-paste attacks.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds SEEK parameter comparisons and text-quality results covering biomedical and legal datasets.

M1.justification: SEEK retains equivalent texture keys, sub-vocabulary decomposition, cipher construction, logit biasing and detection procedures. Algorithm 1 now specifies partitioning using the existing secret key, clarifying an implementation detail without establishing a changed underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Figure 6 adds PubMedQA and FreeLaw to text-quality evaluation, extending coverage to biomedical and legal text; Table 4 also reports PubMedQA diversity results. The existing scrubbing and spoofing datasets and attack tasks remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding scrubbing and spoofing comparisons retain their KGW comparator sets. The added diversity table uses UNIGRAM and KGW-Min, already evaluated in v1 Figure 3; different hash-space sizes are configuration changes. Removed SEEKL rows concern the proposed method's configuration.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the stated perplexity oracle from OPT-2.7B to LLaMA2-13B, and Appendix F.1 changes the default generation limit from 250 to 150 tokens. V2 introduces a six-configuration h/d evaluation on a C4-Eval subset and removes reported h=d=16 evaluations. Figure 6 explicitly specifies gamma=0.25 and delta=2.0. These materially revise reported evaluation conditions without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 3 examines sensitivity to joint and unequal watermark-window/hash-space sizes. Table 4 extends the diversity analysis across configurations and datasets. Conversely, SEEKL evidence is removed from the main scrubbing comparison and Appendix B's model and beam-search analyses, while the remaining robustness analyses persist.

E5.justification: The added checklist states that experimental results were tested multiple times, providing repetition information absent from v1. It supplies no run counts, seeds or uncertainty-estimation procedure, and does not establish an increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: V2 replaces Figure 6's quality distributions, adds parameter-sensitivity and diversity results in Tables 3–4, and removes SEEKL results from three tables. In Table 2, SEEK's C4/DeepSeek AUROC, TP@1% and TP@5% change from 98.0/69.8/91.4 to 98.2/75.0/90.1. Headline scrubbing gains also change. The revised quality plots cannot establish same-setting improvements because the reported oracle and settings differ; spoofing tables retain their numerical entries.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, propositions, assumptions and derivations in Sections 3–4 and Appendices C–D are retained. Equation and proof movements reflect pagination rather than revised mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract changes 'breaks this trade-off' to 'expands the trade-off boundary' and removes its numerical performance summary. The introduction revises claimed C4/LFQA scrubbing gains from 6.4%/24.6% to 13.4%/8.6%. The central equivalent-key mechanism, SEEK contribution and Pareto-improvement claim remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly advises against excessively disparate h and d because the design can become effectively context-independent. A footnote explicitly qualifies reduced-hash-space spoofing resistance at d=1. The explanation that SEEKL makes spoofing samples difficult to collect is removed; the substantive limitations and impact discussions in Appendices G–I remain.

D1.justification: V2 specifies secret-key-based vocabulary partitioning, identifies Figure 3's C4 subset, and supplies watermark parameters for Figure 6 and Table 4. Appendix F.1 removes the repetition-penalty value of 1.2 without establishing that its use stopped. The checklist adds a code-release promise but no concrete access location.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Datasheet for the Pile and Collective Classification in Network Data alongside the expanded dataset discussion. Section 2 and Appendix A retain their substantive related-work discussion and research positioning. The new PubMedQA citation points to the latter reference, leaving an apparent attribution mismatch.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the abstract, adds brief experimental explanations, acknowledgements and a NeurIPS checklist, and updates author and conference information. The main narrative and appendix organization remain largely intact; the added checklist does not constitute extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially revised: two tables are added, Figure 6 is redrawn with different grouping and legends, Table 2's attack blocks are reordered, and SEEKL rows are removed. Spoofing tables and Algorithm 2 are relocated. Most other figures retain their original graphics.

improvement.justification: The h/d sensitivity study and biomedical/legal quality evaluations add useful evidence. However, removing SEEKL results leaves Appendix B.2's highest-performance claim unsupported, while Figure 6 loses model identities despite retaining a two-model caption. Revised settings and inconsistent headline gains further complicate interpretation. These additions and reporting regressions prevent a reliable judgment of the net change in overall quality.
